title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre - Stanford University on 1982-10-09
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/88.2k) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sony ECM-220T -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Fuji Metal Tape/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear audience recording of a Stanford dayshow that captures superb sound but a shaky performance, with The Other One and Morning Dew standing out.
ai_review.review: The tape is praised as an almost‑stereo board‑quality audience capture – crisp, detailed and one of the best‑sounding 1982 Aud recordings. Musically the night is divisive: several reviewers note sloppy playing, tired vocals and botched transitions, yet a few highlights (The Other One, Morning Dew, Throwing Stones) keep it worth listening to.

ai_rating.rationale: Recording quality is consistently rated excellent, but show performance is described as below average by most reviewers; weighting the strong tape against the weak playing yields a mid‑range score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear stereo‑like audience tape, often compared to a soundboard. Phil's bass and Brent's early‑80s electric piano are low in the mix, but overall clarity and detail are superb.

standout_songs: Throwing Stones > Touch of Grey (some enjoy)
poor_songs: Throwing Stones > Touch of Grey (criticized by some)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as flat and plain; second set uneven with a few high points but overall lacking tightness. Transitions feel disjointed for many listeners.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mixed: some say his voice is blown, guitar tired and forced; others note clear lead articulations and good tone on this tape.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass low in the mix with little punch; occasional Fender Jazz bass noted as unsuitable for his style.
band_member_comments.Bob: Criticized for wrong notes and over‑dramatic singing by several reviewers, but also praised for rhythmic interest and being audible thanks to the great tape quality.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent using an early‑80s electric piano that sounds like a cheap Casio; missing Rhodes/B‑3 organ is lamented, though the keyboard is clear in the mix.
